title: 2021 Fall AMC 10A Problem 6
statement: Elmer the emu takes \(44\) equal strides to walk between consecutive telephone poles on a rural road. Oscar the ostrich can cover the same distance in \(12\) equal leaps. The telephone poles are evenly spaced, and the \(41\)st pole along this road is exactly one mile (\(5280\) feet) from the first pole. How much longer, in feet, is Oscar’s leap than Elmer’s stride?

solutions.text:
There are \(40\) gaps between the \(1\)st and \(41\)st pole, which means that the distance between consecutive poles is \[ 5280 \div 40 = 132 \] feet.

This means that each of Elmer’s strides is \[ 132 \div 44 = 3 \] feet. Similarly, each of Oscar’s leaps is \[ 132 \div 12 = 11 \] feet. This makes Oscar’s leap \(11 - 3 = 8\) feet longer.

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: There are \(40\) equal pole gaps in one mile
Find one pole gap, then divide it by \(44\) and by \(12\)
